history.dynasty: Chand (rulers of Kumaon; reconstruction under Uday Chand and Hari Chand)
history.period: 10th-12th centuries CE (per Wikipedia infobox); 13th-century construction (1390 CE by Garud Gyan Chand) also claimed
history.summary: Ancient Shiva temple complex in Champawat town, famous for its stone carving. DATE CONFLICT: Wikipedia's infobox dates it to the 10th-12th centuries under the Chand dynasty, while its text cites a belief that Garud Gyan Chand built it in 1390 CE, with reconstruction by Uday Chand (1420-1421) and Hari Chand (1423-1427, copperplate inscription of 1423 CE) (verify). The compound holds the main Baleshwar shrine plus Ratneshwar and Champawati Durga temples, with carved exteriors and a nearby naula (freshwater spring); a crowded fair is held on Mahashivratri. Maintained by the Archaeological Survey of India since 1952 (designated national heritage monument). CSV state correction: the state column holds town names; the real state is Uttarakhand (town Champawat is correct).

name: Baleshwar Temple
town_description: Champawat is the historic former capital of the Chand dynasty in Kumaon, Uttarakhand, set amid forested hills. It is rich in medieval temples, including the Baleshwar complex and Kranteshwar Mahadev.

travel.road: Well connected by motorable roads from Tanakpur, Haldwani and other Kumaon towns; temple is within Champawat town

visitor_information.best_time: April to June (pleasant summer); September to November (clear mountain views)
visitor_information.opening_hours: Dawn to evening (typically reported 6:00 AM-8:00 PM; exact hours shift seasonally - verify locally)
